rationale: The candidate reads as a slender diagonal connector over a shared low base, so the dominant gesture is understandable. However, the form depends heavily on layered overlap and several clipped protrusions, which weakens hierarchy and makes the mass feel somewhat assembled from pieces rather than one controlled volume. In all four views, the silhouette leans on a stepped/terraced logic more than a singular non-stair mass, and the open/void condition is present only as incidental gaps rather than a deliberate public undercut or courtyard. The volumes also appear to interpenetrate and collide in ways that may be fragile under repair, though the overall diagonal-section idea resonates with the OMA/bridge precedents without directly copying them.
warnings: The form may collapse into a series of thin fragments if simplified further.
Several elements read as overlapping solids rather than a clean primary/support split.
The open space is not yet legible as a meaningful public void.
